_comment: How each model family is told to reason.
Nothing here describes how to *start* vLLM: --tool-call-parser and
--reasoning-parser are flags on your own `vllm serve` command line, and MIMIR
never sends them.
THE DEFAULT COVERS MOST MODELS. MIMIR sends chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking,
which thinking-capable chat templates read and other templates harmlessly ignore.
Qwen3 and its derivatives work this way and need no entry. The served name is
whatever --served-model-name says, so an unlisted name is the normal case, not an
error: it still gets its reasoning.
AN ENTRY IS A DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION. Add one only for a family whose published
behaviour differs, and say in `note` where that was verified -- the default
already works, so an entry added on a hunch can only make things worse.
thinking: 'directive'  the family reads a trained-on line from the system
message and has no thinking kwarg. Give both strings in
thinking_directive.
thinking: 'effort'     the family names a rung in a request param instead.
effort_param       param carrying the rung (default 'reasoning_effort').
effort_levels      the family's OWN ladder, weakest first. Ladders are not
universal -- low/medium/high is OpenAI's, while DeepSeek
and GLM use low/high/max -- and an unknown value lands
on the template's fallback, silently ignoring the pick.
toggle_param       param that switches reasoning off, where the family has
toggle_values      one, with its {on, off} values. Without it the family
always reasons and the panel drops its 'off' rung.
MATCHING is the longest key that prefixes the model name, its last path segment,
or any segment -- so 'gpt' matches 'openai/gpt-oss-120b'. '_' and '.' are the same
separator, so one family key covers 'Llama-3_1-...' and 'Llama-3.1-...' alike.
Two optional per-model knobs are also read from here and unset by default:
max_tools (cap on tools exposed per query) and enforcement ('strict'|'light'|'off').

deepseek-v4.note: Verified in the model card and encoding/README.md of DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813: the release ships no Jinja chat template, reasoning_effort takes low/high/max (realised as a prompt prefix), and thinking_mode='chat' closes the think block so no reasoning is produced. It does not read enable_thinking. Earlier DeepSeek lines are not covered by this key and fall back to the default.

glm-5.3.note: Verified in GLM-5.3-Flash's chat_template.jinja: `reasoning_effort if ... in ['low','high'] else 'max'`. Only low and high are selectable -- anything else, including OpenAI's 'medium', silently becomes 'max'. The template always emits a Reasoning Effort line, so reasoning cannot be switched off. Earlier GLM lines are not covered by this key.

gpt.note: gpt-oss reasons over harmony channels. Its template takes reasoning_effort on the OpenAI low/medium/high ladder and ignores enable_thinking; there is no way to switch reasoning off.

openai.note: Same family under its publisher prefix, e.g. openai/gpt-oss-120b.

llama-3.1-nemotron.note: NVIDIA's Llama-Nemotron series (Nano 8B, Super 49B, Ultra 253B) is trained to switch on these exact system-message lines. Verified on the published tokenizer_config: its chat template reads NO thinking variable at all and passes the system message through, so the line is the only switch. This is NVIDIA's post-training convention, not a Llama one -- stock Meta Llama 3.x does not reason and must not get the directive.
